title: Add RAG agent quickstarts, tool-calling examples, and docs site updates
author: Ava Chen
description:
This PR adds a set of RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) agent quickstarts, agent templates, and tool-calling examples to the docs site and redwood-examples repo. Motivation: provide opinionated, production-oriented examples that show how to wire up Redwood's API + embeddings + a simple retriever and how to use tool-calling within an agent loop. The goal is to reduce onboarding friction for engineers building RAG/agent-based features and to standardize recommended patterns (retriever interface, prompt templates, response schema, and safe tool usage).

What this PR includes:
- new quickstarts under redwood-examples/rag-agent-quickstarts: Python and TypeScript samples that show end-to-end flows (indexing, retrieval, prompt templates, running agent with tool calls).
- agent templates under redwood-docs/content/guides/agents/templates: curated prompt templates for QA, summarization, and multi-step workflows with explicit tool-call hooks.
- docs site navigation and tutorial pages: new /docs/guides/rag-agents quickstart and an examples gallery entry.
- updated SDK examples: small helper in redwood-sdk-python/examples/rag_runner.py and a TS example in redwood-sdk-typescript/examples/agent-runner.ts.
- CI/lint fixes for docs markdown style and code block language tags.

Checklist:
- [x] Add quickstart code and README for Python and TS
- [x] Add agent prompt templates + JSON schema examples
- [x] Update docs nav and gallery entries
- [x] Run docs build and fix lint warnings
- [x] Add basic unit test for example retriever in redwood-examples test harness

Notes on implementation decisions:
- Retriever: examples use a simple in-memory BM25-backed retriever (via the example harness) with clear comments on swapping in embeddings + vector DBs in prod.
- Tool-calling: examples include a safe wrapper for registering tools and a lightweight simulator for external API calls to avoid accidental external traffic in CI.
- Prompt templates: templates use structured output annotations and make explicit when to call tools vs returning final answers.

Related: ENG-1284 (agent quickstart project), PM-372 (docs content tracking), SUP-908 (customer ask for tool-calling example).
